subject: fossa
title: Lemurs Can't Escape This Predator in the Trees

scenes.text: Lemurs can't escape this predator by climbing, because it hunts in the trees.
The fossa of Madagascar is about six feet long counting its tail, which balances it between branches.
Its ankles are so flexible that its hind feet turn nearly backward.
That lets it come down a tree trunk headfirst, and leap from tree to tree.
Hunters can work in pairs: one chases lemurs through the trees while the other waits below.
Lemurs can run, leap and climb, and the fossa follows anyway.

description:
The fossa of Madagascar hunts lemurs high in the trees, using ankles flexible enough to climb down headfirst.
Pairs can even chase lemurs between trees while a partner waits below.
Which predator would you least want to meet? Tell us below.
first_comment: Would you try to outrun a fossa? Tell us below.
